observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 23 that the United States and Iran held their first shuttle talks for months. Neither side announced a change in its negotiating position or a ceasefire.

Reuters shipping data showed three commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday September 22, down from four a day earlier and below the roughly 15-vessel 10-day moving average. The data are preliminary because some vessels may disable transponders.
Reuters reported Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West pipeline, improving the Gulf crude-supply outlook.
Brent traded below $100 during September 23 Reuters reporting, but this is market-price evidence rather than proof that physical shipping has normalized.
semantic_interpretation: Diplomatic optionality improved materially versus the prior snapshot because indirect talks actually occurred, reducing near-term energy tail risk at the margin. This is not a ceasefire or Hormuz normalization event: observed vessel traffic remains severely impaired and neither side announced a substantive change in position. Treat diplomacy as a de-escalation signal while retaining a high energy/shipping risk premium.
